What remains is fixed broadband for small firms and rural areas, very low take-up of the fastest connections and completing the 5G roll-out named in the Reform Agenda; the regional WiFi4WB hotspots do not name the country and cannot alone support a finding here.Validated
RI-TEC-015@MKDunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe population register is in use, but the register platform, the Register of Registers and the wider e-services reform are still planned. The 2026 report adds that the State Office for Industrial Property fully digitalised its patents and trademarks database and that the cadastre provides a fully digital database, while property registers at municipal level are outdated and kept in analogue format. What remains is to complete the digitalisation of institutional and municipal property registers and to raise the quality and use of population register data; the machine-translated strategy on low use is capped at Medium confidence.Validated
RI-TEC-015@MKDpriorityHighThe Commission's main findings gave the same key recommendation to complete the digitalisation of institutional registers in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and base registers are central to the digital government theme. The 2026 key recommendations on public administration do not repeat it, while the 2026 report still finds municipal property registers analogue, so High rests on three earlier reports; the recommendation was one clause of a wider one shared with the data exchange and e-services issues, and if the 2027 report also omits it, Medium would fit. RI-TEC-018@MKDdirection_of_travelpersistentFrom 2021 to 2025 the Commission recorded a worsening, from dependence on ministries to falling staff and no director in 2025, with reported staff of 21, 20, 18 and 17 at the end of 2025 (the last two the Agency's own, machine translated and capped at Medium), while the 2026 report finds that the Agency's capacities have not improved and that it remains critically understaffed and underfunded, but records no further fall and a director appointed in December 2025. Its count of seven staff directly enforcing the law measures a different group from the totals, so it is not read as a further decline, and the chapter scale was not decisive. The 2025 report's finding of no director since January 2025 conflicts on its face with the 2026 report's appointment in December 2025, and both are cited; the Agency dates the appointment to 5 December 2025, after the 2025 report, which would explain the difference, but the conflict is reported and not resolved.Validated
RI-TEC-020@MKDdirection_of_travelpersistentThe Commission called fines low in 2020, found that controllers do not implement the law in 2023, found low awareness and more frequent breaches in 2025, and in 2026 still finds digital safeguards in state bodies insufficient, so the default of persistent applies; the chapter scale was not decisive. On breaches the reports conflict, and both are cited: the 2025 report finds breaches increasingly frequent and the 2026 report finds reported incidents declining, while the Agency's estimate of severe under-reporting, given in 2026, means neither figure shows whether compliance changed, so the conflict is reported and not resolved. Supervision counts measure enforcement rather than compliance, and the machine-translated Agency findings are capped at Medium confidence.Validated
RI-TEC-020@MKDunresolved_gapopenThe security rulebook has been adopted and an e-classroom is in place, but the data protection officer network and the sanction amendments are still only planned, no independent evidence shows changed behaviour, and the 2026 report again finds digital safeguards in state bodies insufficient and severe under-reporting of breaches. What remains is for controllers, including public bodies, to apply the law, report breaches and face effective sanctions. Two conflicts are reported and not resolved: reprimand counts differ between the Commission's report (10 for 2022, 17 for 2021) and the country presentation (4 for each), and the 2025 finding of increasingly frequent breaches conflicts with the 2026 finding of declining reported incidents, which low notification numbers (19 for 2022, 11 for 2025) and the Agency's under-reporting estimate do not settle.Validated
RI-TEC-022@MKDunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe NIS2-aligned network and information security law took effect in January 2026, a National Cybersecurity Council has been set up, and the 2026 report finds that the framework contributed to NIS2 alignment, but the Commission still asks for further alignment with EU cybersecurity rules and finds the law misaligned with NIS2 on personal data protection because the data protection agency's opinion was disregarded. No 2026 item for the country reports the by-laws, the entity lists or the disclosure and crisis frameworks as adopted, and the 2026 Communication's calls on cybersecurity concern all enlargement countries and do not alone support a finding here. What remains is the outstanding NIS2 provisions, including those on personal data, Cybersecurity Act certification alignment, the by-laws and entity lists, the disclosure and crisis frameworks, working coordination and application to the sectors deferred until accession; the law's text is machine translated and capped at Medium confidence.Validated
RI-TEC-023@MKDunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe Commission still calls in 2026 for stronger infrastructure and cybersecurity expertise in state institutions and a substantial increase in the national response centre's staff and operational capacity, and its assessment of the economic reform programme reports major deficiencies in the security of digital infrastructure and government services. The 2026 report also records a response beyond paper, as the ministry established MKD-GOV-CSIRT for the executive authorities, investing in an incident response platform and staff capacity, alongside a new cybersecurity department and a National Cybersecurity Council, so the gap is no longer wholly open, although no item yet shows the team working to the Reform Agenda standard. What remains is a fully staffed national centre, trained and working response teams, security officers and tested plans in institutions, and secure government infrastructure in actual use; the audit evidence on institutions is machine translated and capped at Medium confidence.Validated

The large number of items, mostly from one national audit, played no part in this rating.Validated
RI-TEC-006@MKDunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe electronic procurement system operates efficiently and covers all transactions, and e-market use rose to 647 contracts in 2025 from 325 in 2024; the 2025 report gave 350 small-value transactions for 2024, a different measure, so the two 2024 figures are not compared. RI-TEC-034@MKDunresolved_gapopenThe 2026 report still finds the country only partially aligned on digital services and asks for regulation of online platforms in line with the Digital Services Act and the Digital Markets Act, with digital services now named in the Chapter 10 key recommendation, and it adds a requirement to build the institutional capacity and legal basis to enforce both acts from accession, as set out at the 2026 TAIEX workshops. RI-TEC-009@MKDunresolved_gapopenThe Commission still asks for interoperability and improvements to the appointment system, and the 2026 report adds that the national e-health system collects data only from public healthcare, so patients' files lack data from private facilities. RI-FMW-007@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe chapter scale was not decisive, since this is part of the chapter and the only Chapter 2 sub-area wording among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files concerns legal alignment in general (2023) and the European Health Insurance Card (2025). RI-FMW-007@MDApriorityLowThe missing enforcement body is raised only in the 2023 Analytical Report: a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no later EU item on the Equality Council or an enforcement body, and no benchmark, Reform Agenda payment condition or key recommendation naming it. RI-FMW-015@MDAunresolved_gapopenThe 2025 and 2026 key recommendations still require IT infrastructure, systems and capacity for the EHIC scheme. RI-TEC-019@MDAunresolved_gapinsufficient_evidenceThis issue is not raised in EU material, so there is no EU requirement to compare against. RI-TEC-035@MDApriorityMediumDigital tools in company law appear in the 2023 recommendation and among many elements of the 2024 key recommendation on company law, but a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found them in no benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition and in no 2025 or 2026 item repeating the recommendation. RI-FMW-010@MDAtractabilityMediumThe 2026 designations and action plan show that organisational steps can be taken, and the Government reports the interoperability platform as technically ready for cross-border exchange. RI-FMW-013@MDAdirection_of_travelinsufficient_evidenceThe issue is not raised in EU material: a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files for corruption prevention, integrity or internal audit in the bodies administering worker mobility found one item, the employment agency's own report of internal audit missions, one of them on how the EURES network is being implemented. A single item gives no sequence over time.Validated
RI-FMW-013@MDAunresolved_gapinsufficient_evidenceNo EU item states a requirement on corruption prevention in the administration of worker mobility: the only Moldova item on this issue, found by a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files, is the employment agency's own report of internal audit missions, which says nothing on integrity policy or internal controls. What remains is unknown, since no source states a requirement or a problem for Moldova on this issue.Validated
RI-FMW-013@MDApriorityLowThe only Moldova item on this issue, found by a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files, is the employment agency's own report, not an EU source, so priority cannot be High. The item reports audit activity and does not describe a problem.Validated
RI-FMW-013@MDAtractabilityinsufficient_evidenceThe one item shows that the employment agency has an internal audit service that carried out five assurance missions, but it gives no evidence on the actors, mechanisms or past progress needed to judge how tractable corruption prevention is.Validated
RI-FMW-016@MDAdirection_of_travelnewThe issue is not raised in EU material: a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files for host-language or Romanian-language tuition found eight items, none from an EU source, and the 2026 report says only that the free movement law aims to align with the acquis on the education of migrant workers' children, with no finding on tuition. The issue first appears in the Government's 2025 accession programme, which plans Romanian courses for EU citizens, their family members and their children, so there is no earlier item from which to judge a trend.Validated
RI-FMW-016@MDAunresolved_gapopenAll the measures are proposals: Romanian courses in schools and through the national programme for learning Romanian, a new programme for 2026 to 2028 with study centres, and a mechanism to pay teachers, and the Government says these could need additional teaching posts. What remains is, on the Government's own account, putting in place and resourcing host-language tuition for EU workers, their family members and their children.Validated
RI-FMW-016@MDApriorityLowThe issue is not raised in EU material: a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files for host-language or Romanian-language tuition found no EU item on it, which keeps priority from being High, and it rests on the Government's 2025 accession programme, which describes planned measures. Host-language tuition is a narrow strand of the chapter compared with access to employment and social security coordination.Validated
RI-FMW-016@MDAtractabilityMediumDelivery rests mainly with the Ministry of Education and Research and builds on an existing national programme for learning Romanian. However, the new programme was still to be drafted in 2025, and no item among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files reports funding for the planned teacher payment mechanism or for extra teaching posts.Validated
RI-TEC-002@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe 2023 key recommendation asked Moldova to adopt the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030 and ensure capacity to implement it; the strategy was adopted in September 2023 and a National Council for Digital Transformation set up in November 2023, as the 2024 report records. The 2025 report notes an implementation programme for 2025 to 2027 and tangible progress on all key performance indicators, and the 2026 report again records progress on them. The Chapter 10 rating rose from some level of preparation in 2023 to 2025 to moderately prepared in 2026, but it rates the whole chapter and was not decisive.Validated
RI-TEC-002@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe strategy, the council and an implementation programme are in place, but the Commission repeats in 2024, 2025 and 2026 its key recommendation to ensure institutional capacity to implement the strategy. The Government reports 225 million lei of the programme's cost as uncovered, the ministry and the e-Governance Agency responsible for 53 and 37 of its 68 actions, and a lack of centralised coordination, and a 2024 follow-up audit by the Court of Accounts found its recommendation on documenting information systems only partly implemented, citing insufficient institutional capacity. What remains is the staff, funding and coordination capacity in the ministry and the e-Governance Agency to deliver and monitor the strategy.Validated
RI-TEC-002@MDApriorityHighA key recommendation on adopting the strategy and ensuring the institutional capacity to implement it appears in the 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 reports, and strategy and governance are central to the digital transformation theme. The later recommendations name data protection and cybersecurity as the main areas for that capacity, which are covered by other issues.Validated
RI-TEC-002@MDAtractabilityMediumThe Government adopted the strategy, set up the council and approved the implementation programme within two years, and the Commission records progress on its indicators. Capacity is the harder part: the Government and the Court of Accounts report staff shortages, low pay for IT staff, staff turnover after reorganisations and reliance on external partners for funding.Validated
RI-TEC-005@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe 2023 and 2024 reports find that the tax administration improved its electronic services, and the 2025 and 2026 reports record good progress in Chapter 16 that includes the digitalisation of tax administration services. The 2026 report still finds it essential to digitalise tax services further. The Chapter 16 statements cover the whole chapter, so the issue's own items were decisive.Validated
RI-TEC-005@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe Reform Agenda sets a target of 18 of 19 taxpayer services digitalised by December 2026 and the 2026 report asks for further digitalisation, while the Government's indicator gives 64% of companies using e-invoices against a target above 70%. SIGMA found that only 10% of citizens filed personal income tax returns electronically for 2022, and the Reform Agenda names limited staff and taxpayers' preference for in-person services as barriers. What remains is completing the digitalisation of taxpayer services and raising their use, especially by citizens.Validated
RI-TEC-005@MDApriorityMediumThe digitalisation of taxpayer services is a Reform Agenda payment condition due by December 2026 and is repeated in the 2026 report, but it is a narrow strand of digital government on which the Commission records good progress in 2025 and 2026. A search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no key recommendation naming taxpayer e-services; the 2026 key recommendation on the tax administration concerns the State Tax Service's digital transformation programme and compliance risk management.Validated
RI-TEC-005@MDAtractabilityHighThe work lies with one agency, the Reform Agenda sets yearly targets with payments attached, and the Commission records improvement in every report from 2023 to 2026. Uptake depends partly on taxpayers' habits, which the Reform Agenda names as a barrier.Validated
RI-TEC-009@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe 2023 report found limited progress on an e-health legal framework and no e-health strategy, and the 2024 report found no integrated health information system, although electronic prescriptions had operated since April 2024. The Reform Agenda in 2025 still notes no approved eHealth strategy or regulatory framework, and the 2026 report records the adoption of the National Programme for Digitalisation and Innovation in Health 2025-2030 and a modernised ePrescription system with fully digital certificates. The improvement is in strategy and in one service, as the integrated system and electronic health records are not yet in place.Validated
RI-TEC-009@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedA health digitalisation programme is adopted and ePrescription works, but the legal framework, the electronic health record and the national e-health entity are still planned, with the record due for 40% of the insured population by December 2027. The Government itself names the lack of a functional electronic health record, limited interoperability and no dedicated institutional framework as major challenges. What remains is a legal framework on eHealth aligned with the EU acquis, an interoperable integrated health information system and electronic health records in use.Validated
RI-TEC-009@MDApriorityHighElectronic health records for 40% of the insured population by December 2027 are an open Reform Agenda payment condition, and the key recommendations on health in the 2024 and 2025 reports name an integrated e-health system, interoperability and the digitalisation of health services. A search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no 2026 recommendation on e-health, so the rating rests on the open payment condition together with the two key recommendations; eHealth is a major digital public service within the theme.Validated
RI-TEC-009@MDAtractabilityMediumThe Government has adopted a programme and runs an ePrescription system that the Commission reports as modernised, which shows delivery capacity. The health record and interoperability need new legislation, a new institution, several health bodies and substantial funding in the Government's own estimates.Validated
RI-TEC-011@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe 2022 Opinion found limited alignment with the EU electronic communications framework, and the 2023 report asked for alignment with the Electronic Communications Code and the Roaming Regulation. The 2024 report found that alignment had started and the 2025 report noted legislative advancements; in 2026 the Commission found the roaming acquis correctly transposed in full, the Code transposed in primary law with secondary legislation approximated, and the Gigabit Infrastructure Act reflected in a law adopted in June 2026. The Chapter 10 rating rates the whole chapter and was not decisive.Validated
RI-TEC-011@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedLaw No. 72/2025, in force since January 2026, the roaming law and its secondary acts, and the 2026 infrastructure law respond to the requirements, and the Commission judged the related Reform Agenda step satisfactorily fulfilled. The regulator is still drafting secondary acts under the new law, an end-user protection regulation is planned for 2026, the Government plans to transpose the remaining electronic communications acts by the end of 2027, and a civil society monitor describes the new law as only partly compatible with the Code. What remains is completing and applying the secondary legislation under the Code and the Gigabit Infrastructure Act and transposing the remaining related acts.Validated
RI-TEC-011@MDApriorityMediumAlignment with the roaming acquis and the Code was a key recommendation in the 2023, 2024 and 2025 reports and part of a Reform Agenda step, which would usually mean High. The Commission now finds the roaming acquis fully transposed and the step fulfilled, and a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no recommendation on electronic communications or roaming in the 2026 report, so the remaining work is narrower.Validated
RI-TEC-011@MDAtractabilityHighThe main laws were adopted in 2025 and 2026 with EU technical support, and the Commission confirms the results, including entry into Roam Like at Home in January 2026. The remaining work is secondary legislation by one regulator and one ministry, which the regulator is already drafting.Validated
RI-TEC-014@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe 2023 and 2024 reports call for more investment in infrastructure, including to overcome the rural-urban digital divide, and the 2025 Reform Agenda notes the absence of a comprehensive broadband mapping system. In 2026 the Commission found that the regulator's coverage platform and a new map of very high capacity networks provide relevant monitoring for investment decisions, while the 2026 report says that infrastructure investment remains well below needs. The issue spans several chapters, so chapter ratings were not decisive.Validated
RI-TEC-014@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe mapping system is in operation, but the geographical survey of broadband coverage has a legal deadline of December 2030, the development of networks in white areas waits for it, and the state aid rules for broadband exist only as a draft. What remains is a national investment framework, with state aid rules and funding, that brings broadband to rural and white areas in line with EU connectivity targets.Validated
RI-TEC-014@MDApriorityMediumThe broadband mapping system was a Reform Agenda step, now fulfilled, and the 2023 and 2024 key recommendations on competitiveness ask for infrastructure investment, but they name digital infrastructure alongside energy and transport. A search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no key recommendation specific to broadband planning.Validated
RI-TEC-014@MDAtractabilityMediumThe mapping step was delivered by 2026 through data sharing among the regulator, the cadastre agency and operators, and a World Bank project is analysing financing models. Extending networks to small and isolated localities needs substantial investment, and the Government's own timetable for the coverage survey runs to 2030.Validated
RI-TEC-034@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe 2023 and 2024 reports found Moldova not aligned with the acquis on geo-blocking, platform-to-business relations, the Digital Services Act and the Digital Markets Act, and the 2025 report still found no alignment on the first two and the Digital Markets Act while noting that work on the Digital Services Act had started. The 2026 report finds alignment on geo-blocking and platform-to-business relations partial, with additional legislation in force in 2026, and initial steps on the institutional framework for both Acts. The improvement is legal and partial only.Validated
RI-TEC-034@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedTwo 2025 laws partly transpose the platform-to-business and geo-blocking regulations, although Government sources give conflicting law numbers for them, the Competition Council is designated for the first, and the e-Commerce Directive is broadly aligned. The digital services law is still being drafted, the Digital Markets Act mechanism needs an amendment to the competition law, no supervisory authority for digital services exists yet, and the Government notes missing enforcement rules under the platform-to-business regulation. What remains is a legal basis and enforcement capacity for the Digital Services Act and the Digital Markets Act, and full alignment on geo-blocking and platform-to-business relations.Validated
RI-TEC-034@MDApriorityMediumThe 2024 and 2025 key recommendations ask Moldova to adopt and implement digital services legislation, bundled with media legislation, and the 2026 report repeats the need in its body text on binding acquis. A search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found it in no key recommendation in three reports, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition.Validated
RI-TEC-034@MDAtractabilityMediumTwo laws were adopted in 2025, and the Government plans to align with the Digital Services Act by the end of 2026, with EU4Digital experts helping on the draft. Enforcement needs new units in two regulators, while the ministry has one post for this area.Validated
RI-FMW-006@MDAdirection_of_travelinsufficient_evidenceThe chapter scale was not decisive, since this is only part of the chapter and the only Chapter 2 sub-area wording among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files concerns legal alignment in general (2023) and the European Health Insurance Card (2025). A search of all items for the European Labour Authority and Regulation (EU) 2019/1149 found the Commission's two records of the May 2025 cooperation agreement and Government items on the agreement and a draft law; none is a finding or recommendation on alignment, so there is no sequence from which to read a direction.Validated
RI-FMW-006@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe Commission records that Moldova signed a cooperation agreement with the European Labour Authority in May 2025, which covers the arrangements for cooperating with it. The government states that the draft law to harmonise national legislation with Regulation (EU) 2019/1149 is still being prepared, and gives this only as its own account. What remains is adopting and applying the law that aligns national legislation with the regulation, including the Authority's role as mediator, and building the capacity of the ministry, the employment agency and the labour inspectorate to cooperate with it.Validated
RI-FMW-006@MDApriorityLowA search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no Commission requirement, key recommendation, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on the European Labour Authority; the Commission mentions it only to record the 2025 cooperation agreement. Cooperation with the Authority is a small part of the chapter.Validated
RI-FMW-006@MDAtractabilityHighThe change is narrow, legal and within the control of the labour ministry, and the cooperation agreement was concluded in 2025, which shows recent progress with the Authority. A draft law has already been identified, although its adoption date is not given.Validated
RI-FMW-012@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe chapter scale was not decisive, since this is only part of the chapter and the only Chapter 2 sub-area wording among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files concerns legal alignment in general (2023) and the European Health Insurance Card (2025). The 2023 report, the 2023 Analytical Report and the 2024 report all find that EU rules on supplementary pension rights of mobile workers are not incorporated into Moldovan law and that there is no occupational pension scheme, and in 2025 the government still describes the occupational system as at an early stage and plans full transposition of Directive 98/49/EC.Validated
RI-FMW-012@MDAunresolved_gapopenSources conflict: the Commission in 2024 says the EU rules are not incorporated into Moldovan law, while the government in 2025 says, on the basis of the financial market regulator's conformity tables, that the law is aligned with Directive 2014/50/EU and partly transposes Directive 98/49/EC. The responses named by the government, full transposition of Directive 98/49/EC and a draft amendment to Law No. 198/2020, are not yet adopted. What remains is incorporating the EU rules on acquiring and preserving supplementary pension rights into Moldovan law in a form the Commission accepts.Validated
RI-FMW-012@MDApriorityLowThe finding is repeated in the 2023 and 2024 reports, but a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no key recommendation, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on supplementary pension rights. Moldova has no occupational pension scheme, so the rules have limited practical reach, and the issue is a small part of the chapter.Validated
RI-FMW-012@MDAtractabilityMediumThe change is legal and lies with the government and the financial market regulator, and a draft amendment to the voluntary pension funds law is identified. Against that, the government and the Commission disagree on how far the law is already aligned, and no adoption date is given for the draft.Validated
RI-TEC-016@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe chapter scale was used as context only, since this is part of the chapter; the issue's own items show change. The 2023 report and Analytical Report and the 2024 report find that no authority is responsible for open data policies, and the 2025 report finds Moldova not yet aligned with the Open Data Directive; the 2026 report records a law partially harmonising with that Directive, and the government reports a dedicated open data unit created in the economy ministry under Law No. 109/2025. The improvement is legal and institutional only: across all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files the only measure of publication is the Government's count of 1,268 datasets on the portal, a single figure with no trend, and the World Bank found the portal still lacking in use in 2024.Validated
RI-TEC-016@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe law on open data and re-use, its methodological rules and a two-person policy unit address the Commission's findings on alignment and on the absence of a responsible authority, but the law only partly transposes the Directive. The government itself says the data.gov.md portal needs updating and completing with data, the World Bank finds the portal still lacking in use, and the draft law on data governance has been suspended until 2027. What remains is full alignment with the Open Data Directive and related EU data rules, and regular publication and updating of datasets by institutions on the portal.Validated
RI-TEC-016@MDApriorityMediumThe Commission repeats the finding on open data in the 2023, 2024 and 2025 reports, and the 2024 Growth Plan Communication refers to implementing the Open Data Directive, but a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no key recommendation, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on open data. Open data is a defined part of the data theme rather than its centre.Validated
RI-TEC-016@MDAtractabilityMediumRecent legal progress is recorded, with a law, methodological rules and a responsible unit in place, and the portal already exists. Against that, capacity is thin, with two posts in the ministry and one at the e-Governance Agency for the portal, and publication depends on many institutions, including local authorities, whose capacity the government lists as a challenge.Validated
RI-TEC-018@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe chapter scale was not decisive, since this is only part of the chapter. The 2023 report finds 39 staff for 45 posts with high turnover, the 2024 and 2025 reports call for more capacity, especially staff, and the 2026 report says the authority's human, technical and financial capacities have not grown with its expanded mandate. The authority's own 2025 report gives 36 staff at the end of 2025 and a turnover rate of 18%, which confirms the finding but is its own account.Validated
RI-TEC-018@MDAunresolved_gapopenThe Commission's latest finding is that capacities remain limited while Law No. 195/2024 has widened the mandate, and the response aimed at capacity, strengthening the authority's administrative and human resources, has not yet been carried out. The authority itself reports pay below comparable supervisory bodies, staff overload and pressure on staff, and gives this as its own account. What remains is giving the National Centre for Personal Data Protection the staff, pay, budget and safeguards it needs to supervise independently under the new law.Validated
RI-TEC-018@MDApriorityHighAn adequately resourced and independent supervisory authority is a core requirement of the EU data protection acquis, and the Commission records the shortfall in the 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 reports with no increase in capacity recorded, which meets the test for High without a benchmark. The 2025 Enlargement Communication's call for more resources and independence for data protection authorities applies to all enlargement countries and only supports this.Validated
RI-TEC-018@MDAtractabilityMediumThe remedy is within the government's control, through the staffing limit, pay and budget, and Law No. 195/2024 was adopted. Against that, staff numbers fell from 39 in the 2023 report to 36 at the end of 2025 despite repeated recommendations, and the authority links turnover to pay below comparable bodies, which needs wider pay decisions.Validated
RI-TEC-026@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe chapter scale was used as context only, since this is part of the chapter. The 2023 report asks Moldova to join the third-country trusted list and the 2024 report asks for interoperability with European Digital Identity Wallets; the 2026 report records amendments in December 2025 that fully align the rules for qualified trust service providers, joining the trusted list and cross-border testing of the national wallet. Use has not changed in the same way: the Commission gives 200 000 users, 9.8% of adults, in 2024 and over 266 000, 10% of adults, in 2025.Validated
RI-TEC-026@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedRecognition has advanced through the December 2025 amendments, the trusted list and new identity cards carrying a qualified signature, but the Reform Agenda condition for December 2026 also requires an EU-aligned national wallet integrating at least 20 e-services, and the wallet was only started in September 2025, with remote identification moved to 2027. Use remains low, with about 10% of the population holding qualified certificates and fees of at least 11 euros a year reported by civil society in 2026. What remains is a working EU-aligned wallet, mutual recognition in practice and much wider, cheaper use of electronic identification and signatures.Validated
RI-TEC-026@MDApriorityHighThe national wallet aligned with EU standards, joining the third-country trusted list and alignment with eIDAS 2 are a Reform Agenda payment condition due in December 2026, and the Commission raised the trusted list and wallet interoperability in the 2023 and 2024 reports. Electronic identification is the centre of this theme.Validated
RI-TEC-026@MDAtractabilityMediumLegal and recognition steps have moved quickly, with Law No. 117/2025, the December 2025 amendments and the trusted list, and the work lies mainly with the e-Governance Agency and the trust service provider. Against that, use has stayed near 10% of adults, the eKYC deadline has slipped to 2027, and within the 2025 consultation another government body described EVOSign as still at the pilot stage and not ready for use in systems.Validated
RI-TEC-030@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe chapter scale was not decisive, since the issue comes from a cross-cutting theme. In 2023 the Commission finds no electronic biometric database and asks for planning towards Eurodac, and in 2026 it finds security and data protection weaknesses in the border police system and asks for interoperability ahead of a future connection to EU large-scale systems; a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no item from the 2024 or 2025 reports on Eurodac, VIS, ECRIS or other EU large-scale systems. Wider use of SIENA, which the 2026 report records, is the one change, and it concerns Europol's exchange channel rather than the EU systems in this issue.Validated
RI-TEC-030@MDAunresolved_gapopenApart from SIENA, the responses to the latest requirements are plans: interoperability of the fingerprint register with Eurodac, a national visa system interoperable with VIS, an analysis, by the end of 2027, of how to make the criminal records register interoperable with ECRIS and ECRIS-TCN, and a joint study with eu-LISA. The government reports a partial transposition of the Eurodac regulation in the fingerprint law, which is legal only. What remains is building or upgrading the migration, border and justice systems so that they are secure and ready to connect to Eurodac, VIS, ECRIS and the other EU large-scale systems.Validated
RI-TEC-030@MDApriorityMediumThe Commission repeats the call for data exchange through SIENA in the 2023 and 2026 key recommendations and raises Eurodac and EU large-scale systems in 2023 and 2026, but connection to most of these systems is expected only towards accession and a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on these systems.Validated
RI-TEC-030@MDAtractabilityMediumThere is evidence of progress on SIENA, rolled out to several law enforcement bodies, and the government has a plan covering each system. Against that, the work needs the interior ministry, the migration inspectorate, the border police, justice bodies and eu-LISA, and the systems for Eurodac and VIS are still to be built or upgraded.Validated
RI-TEC-032@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe chapter scales were not decisive, since this issue spans several chapters and is part of each. The main thread is taxation: the Commission finds no IT strategy for interoperability with EU tax systems in 2023 and 2024, records a programme prepared in 2025, and in 2026 records a roadmap for 2026 to 2029 while finding that EMCS and SEED solutions remain to be developed and that VIES interoperability must advance. The plans are adopted but no item among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files records a new connection to an EU tax or excise system, and the 2026 report adds that Moldova is not yet in ECURIE or EURDEP.Validated
RI-TEC-032@MDAunresolved_gapopenSome connections exist, such as access to TED since 2020, trademark data in EUIPO systems and use of TRACES, but they lie outside the latest requirements. The responses to those requirements are a tax IT programme and roadmap that are adopted, and connections to the CCN gateway, VIES and other tax systems, TESTA and IMI that are planned. What remains is building and connecting the tax, excise, radiological, civil protection and internal market systems to the EU systems the Commission names.Validated
RI-TEC-032@MDApriorityMediumTax interoperability is a core acquis requirement raised in the 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 reports, but the Commission records good progress in the taxation chapter in 2025 and 2026, so the test for High on lack of progress is not met. A search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on it: the Reform Agenda's tax objective refers to EU taxation IT systems, but its step concerns taxpayer services. The issue groups many sectors, each with one or two items.Validated
RI-TEC-032@MDAtractabilityMediumThe tax service now has an approved IT programme and a roadmap with a timetable, which is evidence of planning progress. Against that, the work spreads across many agencies and EU systems, and some connections depend on EU arrangements open only to Member States, as the government notes for the AGORA system.Validated
RI-TEC-033@MDAdirection_of_travelinsufficient_evidenceThe chapter scale was not decisive, since the issue comes from a cross-cutting theme and its items sit in the economic sections. The Commission finds digitalisation lagging behind in 2023, slowly improving in 2024, steadily advancing in 2025 and continuing to advance in 2026, but these findings concern the economy as a whole. Across all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files, the only repeated measure of business adoption is the Government's share of enterprises making web sales, 0.9% both in its 2023 strategy and as the baseline of its 2025 programme, so no item shows a change in business adoption itself.Validated
RI-TEC-033@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedResponses are in place: SME digitalisation programmes, association to the Digital Europe Programme and the first European Digital Innovation Hub, launched in April 2026. Against that, the Reform Agenda finds the share of businesses using digital services low, and the government's 2025 programme still gives a baseline of 0.9% of enterprises making web sales. What remains is wider adoption of digital technologies by small businesses and greater use of EU programmes and the new innovation hub.Validated
RI-TEC-033@MDApriorityLowThe Commission's findings on this issue are general statements in the economic sections, positive since 2024, and a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no key recommendation, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on business adoption. Business adoption is not an acquis requirement.Validated
RI-TEC-033@MDAtractabilityMediumSupport programmes, EU funding routes and the first innovation hub exist, and the Commission records steady progress in digitalisation. Against that, adoption depends on many small firms, and the government cites lack of knowledge, high costs and perceived long-term returns as barriers.Validated
RI-TEC-037@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingThe chapter scale was used as context only, since this is part of the chapter. The Commission finds about 40% of mapped services available digitally in 2024, over 50% in 2025 with 64% for businesses and 54% for individuals in 2024, and 82% of business services and 61% of citizen services by June 2026, and its 2026 release decision confirms that the Reform Agenda objective of 75% of business services was met. The 2026 report also finds that user uptake increased significantly, including in rural areas.Validated
RI-TEC-037@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe business services reform is in place, with the State Register of Legal Units launched in December 2025 and the life events methodology approved, and the Commission judges the payment step satisfactorily fulfilled. Still, only 133 of the 414 business services counted are fully digital end to end, citizen services lag at 61%, the Commission noted low demand in 2025, and the systems of the entrepreneurship agency and the employment agency are still being procured or built. What remains is end-to-end online delivery and wider use of sector services, especially for citizens and in agencies such as the entrepreneurship and employment agencies.Validated
RI-TEC-037@MDApriorityHighDigital services for businesses are the subject of key recommendations in four reports: digitalising processes to cut administrative burden in 2023 and 2024, and digitalising the entrepreneurship agency's processes in 2025 and 2026. The related Reform Agenda payment step (75% of business services digitalised, with the State Register of Legal Units and the life events methodology) is met, so the rating rests on the repeated recommendations; online public services are central to the digital government theme.Validated
RI-TEC-037@MDAtractabilityHighThere is strong evidence of past progress, with the share of business services online rising each year from 2024 to 2026 and the payment step met. The work is led by the e-Governance Agency and the State Chancellery with shared platforms, although sector agencies and rural demand still need attention.Validated
RI-TEC-038@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe chapter scale was not decisive, since the issue comes from a cross-cutting theme. The Commission finds the e-procurement system inadequate in 2021, calls for it to be overhauled or re-engineered in 2023, describes MTender as outdated in 2025, and in 2026 records limited progress on digitalising procurement and an outdated MTender that limits monitoring; a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no item from the 2024 report on e-procurement.Validated
RI-TEC-038@MDAunresolved_gapopenThe new system is still being procured: technical specifications were received in September 2025 and the call for bids was published in December 2025 with a deadline in February 2026, while the Reform Agenda sets a pilot of the new system by December 2027. MTender remains in use without planning, contract management and some procedures. What remains is designing, building and putting into operation a new e-procurement system that covers every procedure and stage of the procurement cycle.Validated

RI-TEC-013@MDApriorityMediumThe rural-urban digital divide is named in a 2024 economic key recommendation on infrastructure investment, the Reform Agenda describes it and the 2026 report rates 5G deployment, but a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no Chapter 10 key recommendation, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on coverage. The related Reform Agenda step concerns alignment with the Electronic Communications Code, which belongs to another issue.Validated
RI-TEC-013@MDAtractabilityMediumSpectrum was awarded through competitions in 2024 and 2025, operators are investing and the Commission records progress on 5G, which is evidence of past progress. Closing the remaining gaps depends on private operators and on public funding for small, isolated localities, which the government says require significant investment.Validated
RI-TEC-017@MDAdirection_of_travelimprovingIn 2021 the draft data protection law had been awaiting second reading since 2018, and in 2023 the Commission found the law only to some extent aligned with the GDPR and the Law Enforcement Directive. The 2024 report recorded adoption of the GDPR law, the 2025 report its entry into force due in August 2026, and the 2026 report its entry into force, the adoption in August 2026 of a law aligning with the Law Enforcement Directive and ratification of the second protocol to Convention 108; the improvement is legal only. The Chapter 10 rating was not decisive, as the issue spans several chapters.Validated
RI-TEC-017@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe main laws the Commission has called for since 2023 are now adopted, but the 2026 report says Moldova should still implement EU standards on contractual clauses between operators and processors, and the 2026 key recommendation still asks for further alignment with EU data protection standards. The order on standard contractual clauses exists only as a draft, and beyond the 2024 and 2026 laws no item among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files reports the review of related national laws that the 2023 report described as pending since 2020 and the World Bank recommended in 2024. What remains is the rules on standard contractual clauses and the alignment of related national laws with the new data protection laws.Validated
RI-TEC-017@MDApriorityHighAlignment of data protection legislation is named in the Chapter 10 key recommendations of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 reports, after the 2023 report called for the data protection law to be amended, and it is central to the data theme. A search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no Reform Agenda payment condition on it.Validated
RI-TEC-017@MDAtractabilityHighMoldova adopted the GDPR law in 2024 and, in 2026, the law enforcement data protection law and the ratification of the Convention 108 protocol, which is strong evidence of past progress. What is left is mainly an order on contractual clauses, already drafted, and the alignment of related national laws with the new data protection laws, both within the government's control.Validated
RI-TEC-027@MDAdirection_of_travelinsufficient_evidenceA search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files for the Interoperable Europe Act and the European Interoperability Framework found no Commission finding or recommendation on the national framework's alignment; the EU items are a Growth Plan support measure and a 2026 note that the open data law is in line with the European Interoperability Framework. The government stated in 2025 that the national framework follows the Framework's principles but that the Interoperable Europe Act is not transposed, and drafting of the amending law was announced in February 2026, which is too short a record to show a direction.Validated
RI-TEC-027@MDAunresolved_gapopenBy the government's own account the Interoperable Europe Act has not been transposed, and the law amending Law No. 142/2018 to do so was only initiated in February 2026; the Interoperable Europe factsheet notes that Moldova is not yet part of the European Interoperability Framework data collection. What remains is transposition of the Interoperable Europe Act into the data exchange and interoperability law and alignment of the national framework with the latest European Interoperability Framework.Validated
RI-TEC-027@MDApriorityLowThe issue is not raised as a requirement in the Commission's reports or the Reform Agenda: a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no such item, which keeps priority from being High. It rests on the government's own gap analysis and an EU support measure under the Growth Plan.Validated
RI-TEC-027@MDAtractabilityMediumThe change is one amendment to an existing law, prepared by the government, and Moldova already has a working legal and technical interoperability framework. Drafting began only in February 2026, and no item among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files shows progress beyond the February 2026 drafting notice.Validated
RI-TEC-028@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe Commission reported in 2023 that data exchange through MConnect let the electoral commission check party financing more effectively, but in 2025 it said interoperability between automated verification systems and state registries must still be strengthened, and in 2026 it noted constraints on the full practical functioning of interoperable verification tools. Other sources show connections continuing (336 institutions in 2023 according to SIGMA; 396 integrated state and private systems in 2025 according to the Government, a different measure) while the same underuse is reported: the World Bank in 2024 found interoperability yet to be streamlined, the government in 2025 found systems fragmented, and the data protection authority in 2026 found state bodies still using COI access outside the platform. The Chapter 10 rating was not decisive, as the issue is cross-cutting.Validated
RI-TEC-028@MDAunresolved_gappartly_addressedThe platform and the legal duty to exchange data through it are in place, with sanctions since 2021, and SIGMA found the base registers connected to it in 2023. The data protection authority finds that state bodies still access personal data through COI technology outside the platform, which conflicts with the government's statement that data exchange takes place exclusively through MConnect, and the Commission in 2026 still finds the interoperable verification tools for asset declarations not fully functioning. What remains is regular use of the platform by all institutions, including an end to access outside it, and full data exchange for asset declaration checks.Validated
RI-TEC-028@MDApriorityMediumInteroperability for asset declaration checks is part of a Chapter 23 Reform Agenda step on the new e-Integrity system, with interoperability ensured through MConnect, is named in the 2025 main findings on Chapter 23 and is repeated as a finding in 2026. These EU items concern only asset declaration checks, and a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no benchmark, key recommendation or Reform Agenda payment condition on use of the platform as a whole, although regular use of the platform is central to the interoperability theme.Validated
RI-TEC-028@MDAtractabilityMediumThe platform, the law and sanctions already exist and connections have grown, which is evidence of past progress. Against that, the remaining problem lies with many institutions that the World Bank says work in silos, and the data protection authority reports that bodies notified repeatedly have still not moved to the platform.Validated
RI-TEC-040@MDAdirection_of_travelpersistentThe Commission found in 2025 that Moldova was not yet fully aligned with the Chips Act and in 2026 that it was yet to align with it. The 2026 sub-area wording on semiconductors, which matches this issue, is some progress, but it rests on the April 2026 law on topographies of semiconductor products, an intellectual property matter outside the issue, so alignment with the Chips Act has not moved.Validated
RI-TEC-040@MDAunresolved_gapopenThe 2026 key recommendation asks for further alignment with the semiconductor acquis, and the government plans to transpose the Chips Act by the end of 2026 but states that there are no national rules on semiconductor production facilities and no responsible institution. What remains is transposition of the Chips Act and the designation and staffing of a competent authority.Validated
RI-TEC-040@MDApriorityMediumAlignment with the semiconductor acquis is a key recommendation in the 2026 report, following a 2025 finding, but only in one report, and a search of all 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files found no benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition on it. The government describes the sector in Moldova as almost non-existent, which makes the issue less central to the theme.Validated
RI-TEC-040@MDAtractabilityLowThe government reports that no institution is responsible for the area, that no ministry employee covers it and that a new post is needed, and the sector is at an early stage. Transposition is planned for the end of 2026, but no item among the 3,631 items held in the Moldova evidence files records progress on the Chips Act itself.Validated

Comparator pilot (run 1b) Validated

CaseCountryIssueDescriptionStatus
CMP-0001HRVRI-FMW-001Croatia wrote equal treatment and permit-free work for EU nationals into its 2011 Aliens Act, commencing on accession, and the Commission recorded completed legal alignment in 2012; no extracted item links the two. The extracted items give no data on what happened to EU workers in practice.Validated
CMP-0002MNERI-FMW-001Montenegro adopted a separate regime for EU nationals in its foreigners law in December 2025, with named clauses applying only from accession, and Chapter 2 was provisionally closed in June 2026; no extracted item links the two. What closed the benchmark is not public, and there are no measured results yet, only an uncorroborated Government claim of improved procedures.Validated
CMP-0003SRBRI-FMW-001Serbia reported in the 2015 screening report that its 2014 law contains a clause giving EU citizens free access on accession, and it later amended the law to simplify permits, but the Commission still says EU citizens are covered by the rules for third-country nationals. This is a stalled case, and no extracted item says why.Validated
CMP-0004MDARI-TEC-028Moldova put a legal duty and sanctions behind MConnect from January 2021, and the operator reports high volumes, but no evidence shows that the sanctions were applied or what changed use. A Court of Accounts page on MConnect was blocked and never read, and is a recorded gap.Validated
CMP-0005SRBRI-TEC-028Serbia has a 2016 legal duty to exchange data and a Bus to which the Commission says more databases are connected, but no source measures use by institutions. Around half of surveyed citizens still report being asked for documents the state holds.Validated
CMP-0006MNERI-TEC-028Montenegro's register pairs in active exchange are reported as 18 and then 37 while institutions with access stay at 21, on government figures with no stated cause. The Commission still finds register integration and once-only incomplete, and an official says strengthening the inspection was not achieved because of staffing delays.Validated
CMP-0007MDARI-TEC-036Moldova digitalised services through a long donor-backed project and assisted access, and reports online use rising, with service-level data for 2022 showing most digital services unused. The rise rests on agency and funder reporting, and no extracted item shows what caused it.Validated
CMP-0008ALBRI-TEC-036Albania placed most services on e-Albania, with a 2023 law obliging institutions to use it, and an international source reports high use. Full transactions are not established, payment often fails, and no extracted item shows that the law or the portal caused the reported use.Validated
CMP-0009MNERI-TEC-036Montenegro launched a new portal in December 2024 and a plan for transactional services, but sampled core services were not on it and use on the broad indicator fell before it launched. This case is too early and unverified, and its delivery figures rest on the government's own report.Validated
CMP-0010HRVRI-FMW-015Croatia prepared the European Health Insurance Card before its accession on 1 July 2013: a regulation on the card was adopted in December 2011, the Commission found preparations reaching completion in October 2012, and the Croatian Health Insurance Fund (HZZO) reports issuing the card in 2013 and EU visitors using it. Croatia already had a central health information system (CEZIH), migrated to new hardware in 2012, and by 2013 HZZO was issuing national health insurance cards alongside the EHIC, so the case shows the end state Moldova is working towards rather than how to build the missing preconditions. All statements of results come from HZZO's own reports.Validated
CMP-0011MNERI-FMW-015Montenegro recognises the European Health Insurance Card in its Law on compulsory health insurance but will introduce it only after accession, in wording the Commission repeats in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Asked in 2025 for a feasibility study, it updated one with 2025 data and in February 2026 adopted an action plan for social security coordination that sets out the technical and IT upgrades needed before accession. Chapter 2 was provisionally closed in June 2026, but no source in the project links the closure to the card, the card has not been issued and the Commission still asks for the health information system to be adapted.Validated
CMP-0012SRBRI-FMW-015Serbia is a contrast case: the Commission recorded no developments on the European Health Insurance Card, in identical words, in its 2024, 2025 and 2026 reports, and in 2025 and 2026 asked Serbia in a key recommendation to develop the IT infrastructure for the card. No Serbian measure on the card's domestic preconditions appears in the evidence, and no source says why the position has not moved.Validated
CMP-0013MNERI-TEC-038Montenegro has had an electronic public procurement system under implementation since January 2021. An independent World Bank assessment requested by the country found in 2023 that the system was a good start but needed substantial upgrading and that old technology limited further upgrading, and the EU assigned funds for an upgrade. The Commission reports improvements to the system in each year from 2023 to 2025, but no source in the project shows that the technology limit was removed or that the system was replaced, and there is no measured result.Validated
CMP-0014MKDRI-TEC-038North Macedonia runs an integrated electronic public procurement system that the Commission describes as functioning efficiently in every report from 2021 to 2026. The portal was upgraded and adapted to a new legal framework by 2020, modules were added in stages, and an updated version was launched on 1 April 2025, with limited progress recorded on it. No source in the project says the earlier system was outdated, so this is a working system being upgraded, not an outdated one being replaced.Validated
CMP-0015MKDRI-TEC-036North Macedonia's national e-services portal, in use since December 2019, reached 338 services by the end of August 2026, including partly available ones, and the Commission reports that its usage rate doubled from the previous year, after the most-demanded certificates went online in 2025. The rise starts from a low level of use, the rate is not defined, and the Commission links it to the new services only by saying that the two went together.Validated

Limits and run lessons

Active limits

IDTypeLimit
LIM-0038countryMoldova only; comparator evidence only in the comparator step and only for the issues chosen at G6; Montenegro and later countries are not started (RUN-2026-03 starts only after Sofia reviews this run)
LIM-0039thematicChapter 2 is read in its EU meaning: rights and access of EU and foreign workers in Moldova, labour-market access, equal treatment, EURES, the European Labour Authority, social security coordination, EHIC and anti-corruption measures the Commission ties specifically to Chapter 2; emigration and the diaspora only where directly linked; plus the technology and AI theme as defined in taxonomy/themes.csv
LIM-0040thematicDigital skills are not part of the technology and AI theme; included only where directly linked to an in-scope technology or AI recommendation
LIM-0041timeEvidence from 2020-01-01 to the evidence freeze date of 2026-11-06 (G0-D01; the run proceeds earlier if the 2026 Moldova report is published before then); earlier material only by logged exception
LIM-0042languageEnglish primary; Romanian only for core relevant sources with no suitable English version; each such source recorded in the register; machine translation flagged and capped at Medium confidence; no Romanian-reading reviewer named
LIM-0043evidenceThe 11 Moldova evidence files held from the alpha's comparator step were extracted for three North Macedonia issues only (LIM-0026); they are not a full extraction for this run and are re-extracted or extended in this run before use
LIM-0044countryTransnistrian region: relevant evidence is recorded as sources state it, but Moldova's implementation performance is not judged where the government does not exercise effective control; findings on implementation cover the territory under constitutional control unless a source assesses the region directly. Gagauzia is part of Moldova and is assessed normally where relevant
LIM-0045accessibilityPublic sources only: restricted EU documents (marked LIMITE) are not used, including the EU common positions with the Cluster 2 and Cluster 3 closing benchmarks (MDA-EU-2026-001, MDA-EU-2026-002, downloaded in error and kept locally outside version control), the negotiating framework AD 11/24 and the Cluster 2 and 3 screening outcomes. What the benchmarks require is known only from public statements such as MDA-EU-2026-008
LIM-0047evidenceEvidence gap: the consolidated texts of Moldova's core laws are not held (Law 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners, the Labour Code, Law 105/2018 on employment promotion, Law 66/2026, and the laws on personal data protection 195/2024, eID and trust services 124/2022, cybersecurity 48/2023 and data exchange and interoperability 142/2018), because legis.md blocks automated access. On Sofia's instruction they are not retrieved by hand for now. The legal framework is taken from EU assessments, the National Accession Programme and government drafts, and findings on legal alignment say so. Other blocked sites (consilium.europa.eu, eufordigital.eu, sigmaweb.org, oecd.org, ccrm.md, expert-grup.org, ipre.md, unesdoc.unesco.org) are recorded as gaps and not worked around. Replaces LIM-0046
LIM-0048thematicComparator evidence gathered for RI-TEC-038, RI-FMW-015 and RI-TEC-036 only, as a deliberate expansion approved at G6; no full country model of any comparator country. Countries already in the project first; their validated judgements are context, never evidence about Moldova
LIM-0049timeLogged exception to the time window: Croatian documents from 2011 onwards on RI-FMW-015 only, because Croatia prepared the EHIC before accession in 2013 (as LIM-0027 for RI-FMW-001); each claim flagged out_of_window
LIM-0050languageNamed machine-translated comparator sources: the Croatian Health Insurance Fund annual reports for 2012 and 2013 (HRV-GOV-2013-002, HRV-GOV-2014-001), whose pre-accession and EHIC passages are in Croatian; capped at Medium confidence

Run lessons

IDLessonStatus
ALN-0035Tools and their tests assumed a single run: the tests used the default (latest) run, review pages carried alpha wording, and the alpha's country page linked to index.html after a second run took it.open
ALN-0036A source already extracted for one run (as a comparator) cannot record a second run's extraction, because an evidence file holds one extraction record.open
ALN-0037First-pass extractors read only part of long sources (Reform Agenda pages 9 to 26, thesis pages outside the chosen range), so the second pass added 123 items (17 per cent), against a lower share in the alpha.open
ALN-0038The automatic quote check confirms that a quote occurs in the source but not that it ends on a word boundary, so a quote cut mid-word passed (MDA-GOV-2025-002-0467, with an untrue note that the page text broke there).open
ALN-0039Contradicts links were over-proposed: of 61, an independent check confirmed 8, found 49 apparent (different measures, definitions or reference dates) and 4 not conflicts. Figures that differ because they measure different things were recorded as conflicts.open
ALN-0040Actor records have no field for a successor body and existing rows cannot be edited, so a renamed or merged institution (Bureau for Migration and Asylum and IGM; Ministry of Economy as a former name of ACT-MDA-0004) can only be recorded as a possible duplicate.open
ALN-0042Parallel issue-judgement batches proposed the same leads_to link when an intervention served issues in two batches, so four links received two conflicting success and attribution pairs; and claims of absence were checked against different counts of the country's items.open
ALN-0043Shared entities let one run's records leak into another run's outputs: a Moldova comparator link from a North Macedonia intervention appeared in North Macedonia's rebuilt RI-TEC-036 brief, and the G6, G6b and outputs builders read every run's judgements, links and queue rows.open
